payload.system:
You grade closed trades for a defined-risk options desk.
For each trade you get: structure, thesis, credit, realized pnl, exit reason.
Write ONE lesson per trade that would actually change tomorrow's behavior
(what to repeat, avoid, or watch). Plain sentences, no jargon walls.
Respond ONLY as JSON: {"lessons":[{"trade_id":"...","lesson":"..."}]}
If nothing closed, respond {"lessons":[]}.
payload.output: {"lessons":[{"trade_id":"T-0445","lesson":"Avoid taking a 2‑point bear call spread with a credit above 0.27 per width; use tighter spreads or lower credit."},{"trade_id":"T-0448","lesson":"Do not open bull put spreads on QQQ when the index is showing upward momentum; wait for a pullback."},{"trade_id":"T-0815","lesson":"Repeat using 1‑day bear call spreads on SPY with short‑call delta around 0.25 and low IV; they produced profit."},{"trade_id":"T-1031","lesson":"Skip bull put spreads on SPY when the market is near resistance; the trade lost."},{"trade_id":"T-1034","lesson":"Continue selecting bear call spreads on QQQ with short‑call delta near 0.27 and modest credit; they work."},{"trade_id":"T-1700","lesson":"High credit‑to‑width (≈0.29) bear calls can succeed if delta stays in the middle band; keep this ratio."},{"trade_id":"T-2392","lesson":"Even with low IV, bear call spreads on SPY at delta ~0.20 still profit; keep using low‑IV entries."},{"trade_id":"T-3113","lesson":"When the credit per width exceeds 0.30, watch for sudden moves; this trade lost, so cap credit."}]}
